questions.q: What does the guest broker talk about when asked about debt in dinars?
o: That demand in the domestic debt market has dropped
That the dinar is about to be devalued
That the banks have closed the market completely
questions.e: In the video: "smanjena tražnja na domaćem tržištu duga još od kraja marta" — demand in the domestic debt market has been reduced since the end of March.

questions.q: How does the guest assess the "huge demand" for Serbia's eurobonds?
o: As populist advertising for the average citizen
questions.e: In the video: "nekakva populistička reklama za domaćeg prosečnog građanina" — a kind of populist advertisement for the domestic average citizen.

questions.q: Roughly what is the price of Serbia's debt (ten-year bonds)?
questions.e: In the video: "Cena našeg duga je blizu 5%" — the price of our debt is close to 5%.

questions.q: Why, according to the guest, is it better for the state to borrow in local currency?
o: Because it's cheaper to print money
Because the debt can be managed relatively easily
questions.e: In the video: "mi možemo relativno lako da upravljamo našim dugom" — we can manage our debt relatively easily.

questions.q: What has the dinar's exchange rate been in recent years, according to the guest?
questions.e: In the video: "imamo stabilan, da ne kažem fiksni, kurs dinara" — we have a stable, not to say fixed, dinar exchange rate.

questions.q: Why must the state borrow constantly?
o: Because of the budget deficit and interest on old debt
questions.e: In the video: "vi morate da se zadužujete, da refinansirate onaj raniji dug koji dospeva" — you have to borrow to refinance the earlier debt that is falling due.

questions.q: What does the guest call the main problem?
o: Interest rates that are too low
questions.e: In the video: "ide onako prilično neracionalno" — it goes rather irrationally.

questions.q: How many euros do citizens keep in banks, according to the guest?
questions.e: In the video: "domaći građani samo u bankama drže oko 17 milijardi evra" — domestic citizens keep about 17 billion euros in banks alone.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.about: Words from the video and their translations

questions.e: Kamata — interest (on a loan).
Refinansirati — to refinance.
Održiv — sustainable.
Budžet — a budget.
Obveznica — a bond.
Tražnja — demand.
Kurs — an exchange rate.
Zvaničnik — an official, a public figure.
Na + locative case: na inostranom tržištu.

questions.q: Banke su blago pooštrile ___ za kredite.
questions.e: Pooštriti + accusative plural: standarde.
U + locative plural: u rukama; "u rukama stranaca" — in the hands of foreigners.
U + locative case, feminine: u lokalnoj valuti.
U + locative plural: u bankama.

questions.q: Cena duga je ___ nego pre mesec dana.
questions.e: Comparative: viša cena — "higher".

questions.q: Nije isto da uzmete ___ kredit i odete na more.
questions.e: Accusative case, masc. inanimate: uzeti potrošački kredit.
Na + locative case: na tržištu.
